topic.readerProblem: A founder or marketer wants to know how ChatGPT, Claude, Google AI and other assistants decide which brands to name when a buyer asks, so they can tell which part of the process they can actually influence.
topic.connection: AEOeye audits whether ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity name a brand; this page explains the memory-versus-search mechanism and shortlist formation behind those answers, using our audit-record benchmark for the shape of answers and its caveats.

assessment: The page separates the two ways an assistant can name a brand (training-data memory and live retrieval), walks through how a shortlist forms, and ranks the signals the evidence supports, labelling our own reading as ours. It rests on vendor documentation (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Search Central), the Chen et al. arXiv comparison of AI search and Google, the Lewis et al. RAG paper, SparkToro's run-to-run variance study and AEOeye's recommendation benchmark with its mandatory caveats. It deliberately does not claim published ranking weights, a per-engine comparison of mention rates, a measured effect of recency, or that citations compound; those claims from the earlier version could not be verified.

sources.supports: Google's generative AI guide (last updated 2026-07-10): AI Overviews and AI Mode use retrieval-augmented generation (grounding) to retrieve up-to-date pages from the Search index and improve freshness; defines query fan-out with the lawn-weeds example; says SEO best practices continue to be relevant.

Claude determines when to search; it searches when a request depends on current or changing information, including organizations, people or products that might have changed, and answers stable-knowledge requests directly.

GPTBot crawls content that may be used in training; OAI-SearchBot surfaces sites in ChatGPT search; the settings are independent; sites opted out of OAI-SearchBot are not shown in ChatGPT search answers though they can still appear as navigational links.

Chen et al. (data collected August 2025): software queries in Canada drew 74.2% earned / 25.8% brand sources for AI search vs 53.8% brand / 31.8% earned for Google; fifty unbranded cola prompts gave major brands 56.3% of ChatGPT mentions (274 of 487) and 67.9% of Perplexity mentions (339 of 499); engines differ significantly in freshness; niche-brand advice; authors call absolute percentages illustrative and warn findings are not permanent truths.

600 volunteers ran 12 prompts through ChatGPT, Claude and Google's AI tools a combined 2,961 times; under a 1 in 100 chance of the same brand list twice and about 1 in 1,000 for the same list in the same order.
Lewis et al.: retrieval-augmented generation combines pre-trained parametric memory with non-parametric memory accessed through a retriever (a dense index of Wikipedia in the paper).
